card.title: The Other Favorite
card.instruction: Treat every sign of attention, trust, and affection as something to compare with what another connection appears to receive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Clare's wedding invitation has a ribbon. Mine has a staple.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're my sister. I gave you the first one, before the ribbon arrived.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So Clare got the version you were proud of.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take my ribbon. I'm the bride.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will Clare know? Otherwise she'll still think you like her more.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 compares invitation trim, A3 reads early inclusion as receiving an inferior version, and A5 needs the rival to witness the bride's compensating gesture.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's first-invitation explanation becomes A3's pride comparison; B4's personal ribbon offer causes A5's concern about Clare's knowledge.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains the sister's early inclusion and B4 offers the bride's own ribbon as a meaningful reassurance.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's generous offer but makes its value depend on the other connection knowing A is favored.

specificity.evidence: A1-B2 establish wedding invitations and a sister-bride relationship, with Clare as the comparison.
